findings.title: 7-Zip History (vendor changelog, 26.02 release entry)
findings.summary_md: Igor Pavlov's official changelog lists version 26.02 as released on June 25, 2026 with the entry CVE-2026-14266: XZ Decompression Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution. The vendor fix therefore predates the ZDI advisory and the news coverage in this story by about three weeks. The same changelog shows 26.01 (April 27, 2026) fixing eight other archive handler CVEs and 26.03 (September 3, 2026) fixing CVE-2026-58052, a Mark-of-the-Web preservation failure.

findings.title: ZDI-26-444: 7-Zip XZ Decompression Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
findings.summary_md: The Zero Day Initiative published this advisory on July 15, 2026 as ZDI-CAN-30169, assigning CVE-2026-14266 a CVSS 3.0 score of 7.0 with the vector AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. It credits Lunbun LLC (Landon Peng) and records that the flaw was reported to the vendor on June 5, 2026, with coordinated public release on July 15, 2026. Crafted XZ-compressed data overflows a heap-based buffer in the processing of XZ chunked data, and the advisory notes the issue was fixed in 7-Zip 26.02.

findings.title: CVE-2025-55188: 7-Zip Arbitrary File Write (credited researcher's prior 7-Zip disclosure)
findings.summary_md: Landon Peng, the Lunbun researcher credited for CVE-2026-14266, published this write-up on August 28, 2025 describing how he found CVE-2025-55188, an arbitrary file write in 7-Zip symbolic link handling, during a CTF. The vendor changelog shows that flaw was fixed in 25.01, released August 3, 2025. His site carries no technical write-up for the XZ bug, so the ZDI advisory remains the only public technical record for CVE-2026-14266.
